name: Are Cabinet-Only and Full-Service Kitchen Estimates Comparable?

mainEntity.name: Can I compare a cabinet retailer’s kitchen estimate with a full-service remodeling contractor’s estimate?
mainEntity.text: Can I compare a cabinet retailer’s kitchen estimate with a full-service remodeling contractor’s estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinet-only and full-service estimates usually represent different scopes. A cabinet retailer may price boxes, doors, hardware, and installation while excluding demolition, countertops, plumbing, electrical, flooring, painting, permits, disposal, appliance connections, and repairs. A remodeling contractor may include those services in one coordinated price. Create a scope checklist and add comparable prices for every omitted service. Confirm whether cabinet installation includes fillers, finished end panels, toe kicks, trim, crown molding, modifications, scribing, hardware installation, and corrections for uneven walls or floors. Ask who measures the space, coordinates countertop templating, handles damaged parts, and schedules other trades. Also compare warranty responsibility and project management. When several companies are involved, determine who resolves delays or installation conflicts. A cabinet-only proposal may still be the right choice for a well-defined project, but its total should be combined with reliable prices for the remaining work before making a decision. Ask both providers to describe the exact finished condition included in their estimates.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not without adding the missing services to the cabinet-only proposal. Compare design, demolition, installation, countertops, plumbing, electrical, permits, flooring, painting, delivery, disposal, and project management. A cabinet price can be lower because it covers only part of the completed kitchen.
